speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether he can provide an update on how many households, companies and businesses currently practise recycling of recyclable items respectively; and (b) how extensively are recycling bins used within our housing estates and public places.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Of those who practised recycling, 91% indicated that they did so via the recycling bins provided by our public waste collectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: As a whole, the non-domestic sector had a recycling rate of 76% in 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Besides the recycling bins in residential estates, there are about 125 sets of recycling bins deployed in public places with high human traffic in the Central-South region of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: And 40.8 tonnes of recyclables were collected through these recycling bins in 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: This is higher than the figure cited in recent media reports, which only covers the National Recycling Programme (NRP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NRP, which provides recycling bins and CCRs to make it convenient for households to recycle daily, is only one means by which domestic recyclables are collected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Other means include door-to-door collection by the informal sector and collection drives at community events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We are making it easier for residents to recycle in order to increase the domestic recycling rate to 30% by 2030, which is one of the targets of our Sustainable Singapore Blueprint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: For example, from 1 April this year, all new non-landed private residential developments above four storeys will need to provide dual chutes for refuse and recyclables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These dual chutes have already been introduced in new HDB Build-To-Order (BTO) flats since January 2014.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: All existing condominiums will also have to provide one recycling bin per block from 1 August this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We also recently announced plans to implement an e-waste management system through the Extended Producer Responsibility approach by 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Ultimately, active participation in recycling by all Singaporeans is key to improving our domestic recycling rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA will continue to engage Singaporeans and non-government organisations (NGOs) via social media posts, educational materials distributed at community and school events, and providing information on NEA's website and NEA's myENV mobile app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We hope that through these initiatives, more will be encouraged to do their part for the environment.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am wondering, what is the impact on the recycling process when items are all mixed together, because there are some recycling bins that allow you to separate items but there are some which allow you to mix the items together.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For the buildings that have dual chutes, one for rubbish and one for recyclable items, I wonder whether it is effective, because, for example, glass bottles that can be recycled, when they are thrown from heights, the moment they reach the ground floor, they shatter into shards.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can better education be carried out for residents who may be confused about the two chutes, thinking that they can just throw rubbish into either one of them?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the commingled recycling bin, our approach to encouraging recycling by households is to try and make it as convenient as possible for them to recycle and, of course, to raise awareness about recycling.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The blue commingled recycling bin is placed at every HDB block and provided to every private landed residential home.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First of all, they do not need to invest extra effort and time in segregating the different recyclables.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They also do not need to make space at home for the different recyclables because they can just deposit the recyclables in the blue bins anytime.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These recyclables will be taken to the materials recovery facility (MRF) where the recyclables will be segregated and brought to the relevant recycling plants for processing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the contamination of recyclables that the Member alluded to for the blue commingled recycling bin, yes, there is contamination of recyclables if they deposit food waste or non-recyclables in the bin.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In this area, what we want to do is to appeal to the public to be gracious and not deposit the non-recyclables in the bins, particularly if it is food waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When it contaminates the recyclables, you waste people's effort in wanting to do their part for the environment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we will also do is to work with stakeholders on the ground, for instance, the Town Councils, to make sure that there are sufficient waste bins around.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are also looking into putting up more prominent labels on the blue recycling bins to tell them "no food and liquid waste” in the recycling bins, and we hope that Singaporeans will be more gracious.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Member is right that if you throw recyclables into the chute, depending on where they land, glass bottles, for instance, might be broken.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But this will not affect the recovery of the other commingled recyclables at MRF.
